idiom_name: tagged union: enum discriminant + union payload + switch
implementation_notes: C has no sum types and no exhaustiveness checking, so the classic structure is written by hand: a `struct` holding an `enum` discriminant beside a `union` of per-case payloads, built only through one constructor function per case (`make_card(const char *number)`) that sets tag and payload together, and consumed by a `switch` over the tag. C11 anonymous members keep payload access flat (`p.card.number`), and the only mechanical completeness check the toolchain offers is a build flag: GCC/Clang `-Wswitch` warns about a missing named enumerator unless a `default` label is present, and `-Wswitch-enum` warns even then. The full class-hierarchy-plus-visitor form remains justified when cases need independent compilation or vtables; otherwise enum + union + switch is the idiomatic C realization.
pitfalls: Reading a union member other than the one last written is undefined behaviour, so tag and payload must always be set through one constructor; a hand-assigned pair is the classic C bug.
The union owns no storage for pointers: a case that keeps a pointer into a dead stack frame or a freed buffer corrupts silently, and `memcmp`-based equality is wrong because of struct padding.
A `default` arm makes `-Wswitch` stop reporting missing enumerators; with `-Wswitch-enum` the check survives, so prefer putting the abort/unreachable path after the switch.
